statements.text: The data centers will be obligated to make sure they pay not only their fair share, but actually a little bit more than their fair share for power

If our permitting processes don't help enable projects versus disable projects… that should scare us as Americans when we're in a race right now to be able to have the best computing power in the world
statements.venue: Columbia Energy Exchange podcast (quoted in Senate press release)

statements.text: And I realized that if we are really going to be an AI power and continue to be the leader in technology, we have got to be able to get power and energy to those AI centers as well as just our general industry.
It's not that we shouldn't be building this stuff. It's that it ought to come with the obligation that the data centers pay for their own power improvements and their own infrastructure.

America's 21st-century ambitions—from leading the artificial intelligence boom to revitalizing domestic manufacturing—rest on an aging physical foundation designed for the 20th century. The United States remains a global leader in innovation and entrepreneurship, but we lose that edge if we cannot build the infrastructure required to support these advances.

America cannot lead the world in energy, AI, manufacturing, and critical minerals if it takes a decade to build anything.

Permitting reform is about restoring American competitiveness, strengthening national security, and lowering costs for families. 

Read my op-ed in The Hill: https://t.co/L0nyiTSOzL

Enjoyed a great discussion with @PHMSA_DOT Administrator Paul Roberti and @ClearPathAction CEO @jharrell this morning on pipeline safety and the urgent need for permitting reform. 

Exciting to see how innovative technology like AI, data analytics, and drones are driving this industry forward.

The United States cannot pursue AI dominance, industrial reshoring, advanced manufacturing growth, and long-term energy reliability while tolerating a permitting regime that is fertile ground for procedural obstruction and endless litigation.

The surge in AI data centers is putting an unprecedented strain on our electric grid, but a broken federal permitting system is crushing our manufacturers, delaying urgent projects, and driving up electricity bills for everyone else.

We need to build, and we need to build now. It’s time to cut the red tape and pass meaningful permitting reform.
https://t.co/MTEdEswbvB

Between AI data centers, manufacturing reshoring, and rapid tech growth, the demand for power in America is only growing. If nothing changes in our permitting process, we will not be able to build out our electric grid to keep up with demand. 

If we want reliable electricity and lower utility costs for American families, we MUST fix our permitting process.

Read more about the American Energy & Mineral Infrastructure Act here: https://t.co/I5Axi1HMwb

America’s demand for energy is only going up, driven by AI, data centers, and advanced manufacturing. Unfortunately, we will not be able to meet that demand if our ability to build is tied up in endless, unnecessary red tape. 

If we don’t fix our broken permitting system, American families will pay the price.

I had a great, candid conversation about trading the boardroom for the Senate floor with @AdamGoodman on the @13thandpark podcast. With just a few months left in this Congress, I’ve got a clear mission and a clock ticking.

Permitting reform isn’t just a technical policy issue – it’s about whether America can still build the infrastructure required to compete globally, power AI, and secure our energy grid.

📺 Watch the full podcast here: https://t.co/YAOhOiLdY1

America’s 21st century ambitions – from AI leadership to domestic manufacturing – rest on an aging foundation choked by permitting paralysis. This gridlock is a strategic threat to our national security. 

We MUST reform our permitting system so American industry can compete and build.

Read my full thoughts in @the535news ➡️
https://t.co/0CM5Z6yWRo

I had a productive meeting today with @HeidiOverton on her nomination to serve as the @FDA Commissioner. We discussed her ideas for how the FDA can keep up with modern pharmaceutical developments coming from AI, and ways to ensure Americans are best served by those advancements.

We are in a fierce global race for AI dominance and industrial power, yet we struggle to build the basic infrastructure to power it. ⚡

Our foreign adversaries are moving ahead while Senate leadership lets petty midterm politics stall permitting reform. We risk ceding our global leadership because we tie our own hands.

America’s ability to build is stalled by red tape — hurting energy security, manufacturing & AI leadership.

I’m launching a series of blog posts on my website highlighting the ways the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) will deliver meaningful permitting reform with broad support from industry, utilities, clean energy groups & policy organizations.

It’s time to get America building again.

https://t.co/suZCq8FPES

America’s ambitions to strengthen energy security, reshore manufacturing, and lead the world in artificial intelligence depend on one fundamental capability: our ability to build.

BAAJA is the solution to get America building again.
